# Purpose {#sec-purpose}

This specimen tests the shared visual language for the course notes before we write the first full lecture. It includes a [beautiful external link](https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/), internal cross-references, mathematics, source code, a figure, a table, callouts, and a scholarly citation.

The design should remain quiet enough for sustained reading while making definitions, examples, and implementation details easy to find.

:::{.callout-note}
## Learning objectives

After reading a course note, students should know what they are expected to understand, implement, and explain—not merely which pages they have completed.
:::

## Mathematical typography {#sec-mathematics}

A language model assigns a probability to a token sequence. Using the chain rule,

$$
P(w_{1:n}) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} P(w_i \mid w_{1:i-1}).
$$ {#eq-chain-rule}

@Eq-chain-rule should be readable inline with the surrounding explanation. For a bigram approximation,

$$
P(w_i \mid w_{1:i-1}) \approx P(w_i \mid w_{i-1}).
$$

:::{.callout-tip}
## Intuition

The chain rule is exact. The approximation appears only when we limit how much history the model may use.
:::

## Code and implementation notes {#sec-code}

Code should fit the page, preserve indentation, and remain visually distinct from prose.

```python
from collections import Counter

def unigram_distribution(tokens: list[str]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Estimate a maximum-likelihood unigram distribution."""
    counts = Counter(tokens)
    total = sum(counts.values())
    return {token: count / total for token, count in counts.items()}
```

:::{.callout-warning}
## Common mistake

A maximum-likelihood estimate assigns zero probability to every unseen token. Later notes will introduce smoothing and explicit unknown-token handling.
:::

| Static embedding | 50–300 | No | Neural representations |

## Checkpoint

Before continuing, a student should be able to explain why the vector for *bank* is fixed in a static embedding but changes across sentences in a contextual model.
:::
